answer: A durable defense is a stake-backed reputation trellis: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can earn, and its standing climbs like a route toward a summit only through attested useful work over time. Fake identities then face a real cost, since each new identity must fund its own stake and wait out the same slow climb, while a shared harbor of peer attestations exposes clusters that vouch for each other in circles. Slashing the stake when fraud is proven turns mass identity farming from cheap into ruinous.
